invariants: Reachable only on data-internal, which is an internal network with no egress. The database is never published to a host port outside the dev stack
Vector columns are 1024-dimensional and a CHECK constraint enforces it; see ADR-002
The image is pinned by digest and must remain a pgvector build. A plain postgres image satisfies every migration up to 0026 and then fails, which is how it was caught in CI
public_interfaces: PostgreSQL wire protocol on the data-internal network
components.purpose: PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension: application tables, the vector store, and the durable embedding cache

invariants: Logical database allocations are explicit and exclusive: 0 general cache, 1 Taskiq broker, 2 Taskiq results, 3 embedding cache level one. A new consumer may not quietly reuse an allocated database
Persistence is on (appendonly with everysec fsync), and its volume is external preserved state this repository did not create
Production requires a password; the base and dev stacks deliberately run without one on an internal network
public_interfaces: Redis protocol on the data-internal network
components.purpose: Cache, Taskiq broker and result backend, and the level-one embedding cache

invariants: The general and RAG buckets stay distinct and are addressed with separate endpoint and credential settings, so a misconfiguration cannot silently merge user media with the RAG corpus
Addressed S3-compatibly through boto3; there is no MinIO-specific client and no MINIO_* application setting
public_interfaces: S3 API on the data-internal network
components.purpose: S3-compatible object storage for uploaded media and RAG source documents

invariants: One instance serves both Docling paths. The ingestion and chat-upload client and the MCP sidecar must resolve to the same URL with compatible timeouts; see ADR-004
Its model cache is an external preserved volume mounted read-only, so a container restart never re-downloads models and no service can corrupt the cache
Models load lazily rather than at boot, so a cold start is fast and the first conversion is slow
components.purpose: GPU-backed document conversion service shared by the ingestion path and the docling-mcp sidecar

invariants: No Compose file declares this. It runs on the host and containers reach it through the Docker-internal host alias, so without modelling it as a component the embedding and reranker dependency edges simply vanish from the graph
It must serve the contracted embedding model at 1024 dimensions; make preflight-model probes exactly that and additionally checks the reranker returns a finite score
It is a single point of failure for both ingestion and retrieval, and it is not restarted or health-managed by any Compose lifecycle target
components.purpose: Docker Model Runner on the host, serving embeddings and the reranker

invariants: Read-only is enforced at three independent layers: the container command flags, the settings-validator allowlist frozenset, and a runtime post-probe assert. Governance cross-checks the three; drift between any two is the finding
The tool allowlist is identical at every layer. Widening it at one layer only is the exact failure this cross-check exists to catch
Image-only: there is no directory anywhere in the repository that could hold an annotation for this component, which is why it is declared here
public_interfaces: MCP over HTTP on container port 8082
components.purpose: Read-only GitHub MCP server available to the agent under the mcp Compose profile

invariants: These edges live in database rows, not in any file. Static extraction cannot enumerate them, so they are recorded only from runtime evidence with provenance database, under the runtime-evidence rules, and never statically assumed

Bearer tokens and the full connection URL are encrypted at rest: because the catalog supports placing a token in the URL, the url column keeps only the credential-stripped form (no query string, fragment, or userinfo) and only the Fernet-encrypted connect_url is ever used to open a connection. Every governance surface still strips query strings and userinfo before storing or logging a URL

Every tool from a user-added MCP server that is not annotated readOnlyHint pauses for the same deferred-tool human approval the Google write tools use. Approval is fail-closed: an unannotated tool is treated as a mutation, so allowed_tools unset widens exposure but never bypasses the gate

The stored URL is SSRF-revalidated at connection time, not only at write time: the per-turn toolset build re-runs the DNS check ahead of the probe cache, and the connection test endpoint revalidates before probing. Deployment-managed sidecar URLs are exempt because they legitimately resolve to internal addresses
components.purpose: Per-user MCP connections: the privileged tool surface that exists only as database rows

invariants: Ownership spans four roots — a route, a component directory, hooks, and stores — which is why it is declared here rather than as a directory annotation: no single directory contains it
This is the one browser surface that talks to the backend directly, over a WebSocket, with the access token passed as a subprotocol so it stays out of query strings and access logs
WebSocket events are untyped dicts with no schema. The compatibility check is the set difference between what the backend produces and what this component consumes
A dropped connection refreshes the access token before reconnecting; a token expiring mid-conversation must not end it
components.purpose: The chat experience: page, components, streaming hook, and client state

invariants: The only service in any stack that publishes a non-loopback host port. Its dashboard is bound to loopback
The HTTP port is configurable because this host already runs IIS on port 80; a hard-coded 80 would collide
Present only under the edge profile of the production stack
public_interfaces: HTTP and HTTPS on the host
components.purpose: Production edge: TLS termination, Let's Encrypt, and host-based routing to the API and frontend

invariants: Spans two roots, which is why it is declared here rather than annotated in either one
The CLI never imports application code in-process; anything that must execute it runs in a scrubbed subprocess
Generated output is byte-reproducible: LF, UTF-8 without BOM, sorted keys, no timestamps. Two syncs with no source change produce no diff
Automation may regenerate derived files and propose changes, but may not weaken a policy, broaden a permission, accept a security exception, or approve its own governance change
components.purpose: The governance control plane: contract, schemas, policies, manifests, history, and the CLI that maintains them

configuration_classifications.name: DATABASE_URL
configuration_classifications.reason: A settings property assembled from the POSTGRES_* inputs. Documenting it as a settable variable — as ENV_VARS.md did — sends people to set something that has no effect.

configuration_classifications.name: DATABASE_URL_SYNC
configuration_classifications.reason: The synchronous counterpart used by Alembic. Same reasoning.

configuration_classifications.name: REDIS_URL
configuration_classifications.reason: Assembled from REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT, REDIS_DB, and REDIS_PASSWORD.

configuration_classifications.name: SECRET_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Signs access and refresh tokens. Curated rather than inferred: it is a plain string field, so no type-based rule would catch it.

configuration_classifications.name: API_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Service-to-service authentication, compared with a constant-time comparison.

configuration_classifications.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
configuration_classifications.reason: Database credential.

configuration_classifications.name: REDIS_PASSWORD
configuration_classifications.reason: Required in production, deliberately empty on the internal network in the base and dev stacks.

configuration_classifications.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Object storage credential for the general bucket.

configuration_classifications.name: S3_SECRET_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Object storage credential for the general bucket.

configuration_classifications.name: S3_RAG_ACCESS_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Separate credential for the RAG bucket, deliberately not shared with the general bucket.

configuration_classifications.name: S3_RAG_SECRET_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Separate credential for the RAG bucket.

configuration_classifications.name: MINIO_ROOT_USER
configuration_classifications.reason: Consumed by the MinIO container and passed through to the S3 settings; it is not a backend settings field.

configuration_classifications.name: MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD
configuration_classifications.reason: Same.

configuration_classifications.name: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: LLM provider credential. A live value was committed and pushed before governance adoption; see the secrets-pushed-to-remote finding.

configuration_classifications.name: LOGFIRE_TOKEN
configuration_classifications.reason: Telemetry write token. Also a live value that was committed and pushed.

configuration_classifications.name: TAVILY_API_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Web search provider credential.

configuration_classifications.name: LLAMAPARSE_API_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Alternative PDF parser credential.

configuration_classifications.name: GITHUB_MCP_TOKEN
configuration_classifications.reason: Injected into the GitHub MCP runtime spec, deliberately kept outside the MCP_SERVERS JSON so the server list can be non-secret configuration.

configuration_classifications.name: BROWSERLESS_TOKEN
configuration_classifications.reason: Shared between the browser service and its MCP sidecar. The placeholder value is rejected by make preflight-mcp.

configuration_classifications.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
configuration_classifications.reason: Login OAuth credential. Typed as a plain string while its API counterpart is a SecretStr, which is precisely why secret classification is curated rather than inferred.

configuration_classifications.name: GOOGLE_API_CLIENT_SECRET
configuration_classifications.reason: Per-user Google Workspace OAuth credential.

configuration_classifications.name: GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_ID
configuration_classifications.reason: Compatibility with preview-MCP variable names, retained while the MCP-to-direct-REST migration completes.
configuration_classifications.removal_milestone: Remove once no deployment sets it and the direct Google REST executor is the only path

configuration_classifications.name: GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET
configuration_classifications.reason: Compatibility with preview-MCP variable names.

configuration_classifications.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_ID
configuration_classifications.reason: Compatibility with names shipped in earlier environment examples.
configuration_classifications.removal_milestone: Remove once no deployment sets it

configuration_classifications.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_SECRET
configuration_classifications.reason: Compatibility with names shipped in earlier environment examples. Distinct from GOOGLE_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS_FILE, which is the service-account connector and is not deprecated.

configuration_classifications.name: DOMAIN
configuration_classifications.reason: Consumed by the production Compose file for Traefik host rules. Not a backend settings field, which is why it appears in the template but never in Settings.

configuration_classifications.name: ACME_EMAIL
configuration_classifications.reason: Consumed by Traefik for Let's Encrypt registration.

configuration_classifications.name: TRAEFIK_HTTP_PORT
configuration_classifications.reason: Configurable because this host already runs IIS on port 80.

configuration_classifications.name: TRAEFIK_HTTPS_PORT
configuration_classifications.reason: Production edge port.

configuration_classifications.name: TRAEFIK_DASHBOARD_PORT
configuration_classifications.reason: Bound to loopback only.

configuration_classifications.name: TRAEFIK_DASHBOARD_AUTH
configuration_classifications.reason: htpasswd credential for the Traefik dashboard.

configuration_classifications.name: CODECOV_COOKIE_SECRET
configuration_classifications.reason: Signs the self-hosted Codecov session cookie. Interpolated into the codecov-api and codecov-worker containers as SETUP__HTTP__COOKIE_SECRET; the application never reads it.

configuration_classifications.name: CODECOV_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID
configuration_classifications.reason: GitHub OAuth App identifier for Codecov login. Not secret, but only the Codecov containers consume it.

configuration_classifications.name: CODECOV_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET
configuration_classifications.reason: GitHub OAuth App secret for Codecov login.

configuration_classifications.name: CODECOV_GLOBAL_UPLOAD_TOKEN
configuration_classifications.reason: Instance-wide upload token; anyone holding it can upload a report for any repository on the instance. Empty by default so the feature is off until deliberately enabled.

configuration_classifications.name: CODECOV_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
configuration_classifications.reason: HMAC secret Codecov uses to verify GitHub webhook deliveries.

configuration_classifications.name: CODECOV_POSTGRES_PASSWORD
configuration_classifications.reason: Credential for Codecov's own PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB containers, distinct from the application database.

configuration_classifications.name: CODECOV_MINIO_ROOT_USER
configuration_classifications.reason: Root credential for Codecov's own MinIO archive store, distinct from the application's MinIO.

configuration_classifications.name: CODECOV_MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD
configuration_classifications.reason: Same.

configuration_classifications.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
configuration_classifications.reason: Present in the backend template under the embeddings section but absent from Settings, so it is silently dropped. Either the embeddings client should read it or it should be removed; recorded rather than guessed at.

configuration_classifications.name: ENABLE_CODE_EXECUTION
configuration_classifications.reason: Present in the template but absent from Settings. Code execution is enabled by the generator context flag, not by this variable.

configuration_classifications.name: CODE_EXECUTION_MAX_ALLOCATIONS
configuration_classifications.reason: Present in the template but absent from Settings, which has CODE_EXECUTION_MAX_MEMORY_MB instead. Looks like a rename that left the template behind.

configuration_classifications.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
configuration_classifications.reason: Baked into the frontend image at build time. Changing it requires a rebuild; restarting the container will not pick up a new value.

configuration_classifications.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL
configuration_classifications.reason: Baked at build time. Used by the chat WebSocket, which is the one direct browser-to-backend edge.

configuration_classifications.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL
configuration_classifications.reason: Both a build argument and a runtime environment variable on the frontend service, so the two can disagree.

configuration_classifications.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_RAG_ENABLED
configuration_classifications.reason: Both a build argument and a runtime environment variable.

configuration_classifications.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_OAUTH_PROVIDERS
configuration_classifications.reason: Baked at build time.

configuration_classifications.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB
configuration_classifications.reason: Baked at build time from the backend's MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB, so the two can drift apart across a rebuild boundary.

configuration_classifications.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED
configuration_classifications.reason: Declared in the frontend template; not passed as a Compose build argument, so it only takes effect for local builds.

configuration_classifications.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
configuration_classifications.reason: Read by the OpenTelemetry SDK from the environment by convention, not through an explicit process.env reference, so no extractor can find its consumer. Classified here rather than left as an unknown consumer, which would be a false positive.

configuration_classifications.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS
configuration_classifications.reason: Same convention-based read as the endpoint. Marked secret because it typically carries an authorization header for the telemetry backend.

configuration_classifications.name: BACKEND_URL
configuration_classifications.reason: Server-side only: the proxy route handlers use it to reach the backend. It is never exposed to the browser, which is the entire point of the proxy layer.

configuration_classifications.name: BACKEND_WS_URL
configuration_classifications.reason: Server-side WebSocket base. The browser uses NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL instead, because the chat socket connects directly.
